_about: Reference properties of mineral SPECIES, not of individual specimens. These describe what is generally true of a species and are shown on a specimen page only as background, clearly labelled. Never use them as evidence of where a particular specimen came from. Key = lowercase species name, referenced from specimens.json → identification.species.

conichalcite.name: Conichalcite
conichalcite.colour: Grass-green to yellowish green, pistachio-green, emerald-green
conichalcite.habit: Typically radial fibrous aggregates, botryoidal to reniform crusts, or massive; euhedral crystals are rare
conichalcite.formationEnvironment: An uncommon secondary mineral in the oxidized zone of copper deposits, typically forming by alteration of enargite.
properties: Forms solid-solution series with austinite (zinc in place of copper), cobaltaustinite, and tangeite.
Commonly colour-zoned when viewed in thin section.
Name from the Greek for “lime” and “copper”, the two essential metals in its composition.

scolecite.name: Scolecite
scolecite.habit: Slender prismatic crystals, often square in cross-section and striated lengthwise; characteristically in radiating sprays or fibrous masses
scolecite.formationEnvironment: Primarily in cavities in basalts; also in gneisses and amphibolites, and in intrusions derived from syenitic and gabbroic magmas.
properties: May fluoresce yellow to brown under ultraviolet light.
Name from the Greek for “worm”, after the way it curls when heated.
Closely resembles the related fibrous zeolites natrolite and mesolite; telling them apart reliably usually needs optical or X-ray methods.

fluorite.name: Fluorite
fluorite.specificGravity: 3.175–3.184 (measured); up to 3.56 if rich in rare-earth elements
fluorite.colour: Colourless, white, purple, blue, green, yellow, orange, red, pink, brown or bluish black; commonly colour-zoned
fluorite.habit: Cubes and octahedra (rarely dodecahedra) or combinations; also nodular, botryoidal, granular or massive
fluorite.formationEnvironment: An accessory mineral in granites, granite pegmatites, syenites, carbonatites and alkaline intrusives, and around fumaroles; economic deposits form in low- to high-temperature hydrothermal veins and stratabound deposits, and it can cement sandstones.
properties: Fluoresces blue, violet, green, yellow or red under UV light; may also be phosphorescent, thermoluminescent or triboluminescent.
Isotropic: light travels at the same speed in every direction through the crystal.
Name from the Latin “to flow”, after its low melting point.
